title: A Memory Engine Stops a Kids App From Repeating Itself | vitalii.no
description:
How a family homeschool app learned to stop repeating the same colors, animals and lessons to five kids — and what changed when its memory finally covered the AI too.

A re-render of two days of worksheets for one child showed the exact same structure every time: the same six colors, the same pig three days running, one fixed math template. A wider audit of all five kids found the AI-generated daily routine repeating itself too — identical grammar sentences two days apart, one gap-fill answer served ten times in thirteen days, one topic running fourteen days straight.

Every item builder for the early-grade engine now draws from a rolling list of each child's last 120 skills and tags, stored in Supabase, always pulling unseen material first from a pre-shuffled pool. Bonus math makers rotate across days instead of always restarting from the top. For the AI-driven daily sets, a 7-day digest of recent words, answers, openers, names and lesson topics is sent to the model as a hard ban list for today's set.

Toddler and early-grade item banks grew alongside the fix, and the Ukrainian spaced-repetition track now advances after ten days even on a weak step, instead of stalling on it indefinitely. All three layers of the app now share one rule: never repeat what a child just saw.
